introduction: CEAP helps eligible Connecticut households with heating costs. Applications for the 2026–2027 season are open, with an eligibility-application deadline of May 31, 2027.
description: CEAP helps eligible Connecticut households with heating costs. Applications for the 2026–2027 season are open, with an eligibility-application deadline of May 31, 2027.

sections.who: Connecticut households must meet the season’s financial and heating-assistance rules. A local Community Action Agency can explain how household members, income and heating arrangements are assessed.
sections.get: Assistance usually goes to the utility or fuel vendor. Deliverable-fuel households may qualify for additional deliveries; related shutoff protection or equipment support has separate conditions.
sections.docs:
• Income and household information required for the current season.
  • Heating bill or vendor/account details.
  • Address and rental information, plus urgent shutoff or low-fuel notices.
sections.apply:
1. Find the application instructions

    Use the CEAP How to Apply page for the current online portal and local intake options.

  2. Prepare household and heating records

    Ask the Community Action Agency for its current checklist and explain whether you heat with a utility or delivered fuel.

  3. Apply before the current deadline

    The state lists May 31, 2027 as the last eligibility-application date. Explain any urgent fuel or shutoff problem rather than assuming normal processing can address it in time.
sections.after: CEAP is an annual benefit: apply again each season. Ask the agency about fuel authorization deadlines, which can differ from the eligibility-application deadline.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using CEAP current season; Application instructions. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Yes. The state announces applications for the 2026–2027 season.
Do benefits go directly to me?
They are usually paid to the utility or fuel vendor.

Is the fuel-delivery deadline the same as the application deadline?
Not necessarily. Confirm the authorization and delivery rules with the local agency.
